answers.answer: Shuffle all 4 Conflict III cards and place them face down at the bottom; shuffle all 9 II cards and deal 5 face down above them; shuffle all 3 I cards and deal 1 face down on top. Return unused I and II cards to the box unseen.
answers.evidence: Setup: face-down 10-card Conflict Deck; shuffle-and-deal table.

answers.answer: In either game, a human starts with two Agents on the Leader and the third (Swordmaster) beside the board, three troops in a garrison and nine troops in supply, and 1 water. The starting Score marker is 1 VP in a four-player game and 0 VP in a three-player game.
answers.evidence: Setup, step 6: score 1 in 4-player, otherwise 0; two Agents; three troops and remaining nine; take 1 water.

answers.answer: Yes. You may take a Reveal turn while Agents remain, but after Revealing your turns are skipped for the rest of the phase. Reveal effects come only from cards remaining in hand that you reveal, not cards played on Agent turns. At Clean Up, move all Agent-turn and Reveal cards in front of you to your discard pile.
answers.evidence: Player Turns; Reveal Turn: remaining hand only; Clean Up all cards in front of you.

answers.answer: Resources from a Plot Intrigue played before placement may pay entry if gained before the placement. Effects from the Agent card or destination happen after placement and cannot pay that entry cost. One card sends one Agent using one icon. A card with no Agent icon cannot be used for an Agent turn.
answers.evidence: Player Turns entry-cost timing; Agent Turn: choose only one Agent icon; no Agent icons means Reveal only.

answers.answer: At a Combat space, deploy all three troops recruited this turn plus up to two from the garrison, for up to five total. At a non-Combat space you cannot deploy; recruited troops go from supply to the garrison.
answers.evidence: Recruiting & Deploying Units: recruit from supply to garrison; Combat space deploys recruited current-turn units plus up to two garrison units.

answers.answer: A Spy Agent icon lets you send an Agent to a space connected to a post where your Spy remains; you do not recall that Spy. Infiltrate recalls a Spy from a connected post to bypass another player’s Agent, not your own. Gather Intelligence recalls a Spy from a connected post to draw a card immediately after Agent placement and before space or card effects. The same Spy cannot pay for both; two different Spies can pay for Infiltrate and Gather Intelligence on one placement.
answers.evidence: Spies & observation posts: Spy Agent icon, Infiltrate, Gather Intelligence and same-Spy restriction.

answers.answer: Strength is 11: two troops contribute 4, one sandworm 3, and four revealed swords 4. If the final unit is removed, strength becomes 0. A player with no unit in the Conflict cannot play Combat Intrigue.
answers.evidence: Strength: 2 per troop, 3 per sandworm, 1 per sword; no units means strength 0; Combat Intrigue requires a unit.

answers.answer: Yes. Passing does not bar you from acting again if an opponent plays; the Combat Intrigue window closes after all involved players pass consecutively. After rewards, troops return to their supply (not garrison), sandworms to the bank.
answers.evidence: Combat: may play or pass, not required to pass after earlier pass; window closes on consecutive passes; cleanup destinations.

answers.answer: With exactly two tied for first in four players, each receives the second reward; the other players compete for the third reward, but nobody wins or takes the Conflict card. With the same tie in a three-player game, each tied player gets the second reward, no other reward is given, and nobody takes the card. A player with 0 strength receives no reward.
answers.evidence: Combat ties; three-or-fewer and four-player tied-first rules; Resolve Combat: 0 strength receives no reward.

answers.answer: One or more sandworms double rewards once; having two worms does not quadruple them. Control and battle icons on won Conflict cards are not doubled. For a reward offering 3 spice to gain 1 VP, you may pay the cost a second time: pay 3 spice for 1 VP, or 6 spice total for 2 VP.
answers.evidence: Sandworm Reward Doubling: one or more worms; control and battle icons excluded; may pay cost a second time.

answers.answer: After winning and taking the Conflict card face up into your supply, check for another face-up Conflict or Objective card with the same battle icon. The matching pair must be flipped face down for 1 VP. At Endgame, a wild icon may match any one of the three icons in your supply, also flipping the pair for 1 VP.
answers.evidence: Battle Icons: win, take card, check for same icon and must flip pair; Endgame wild match.

answers.answer: At 2 Influence, gain 1 VP; losing below 2 loses that VP, and reaching 2 again regains it. At 4, gain the printed track bonus, which is retained below 4 and earned again upon returning to 4. First to 4 also gains Alliance and 1 VP, which stays only while holding it. Tying the current holder does not transfer the Alliance; you must rise above them.
answers.evidence: Victory Points—Faction Influence: 2 and 4 rewards; tie does not steal Alliance.

answers.answer: During Reveal, Persuasion may be spent before, between, or after Reveal effects. It can be pooled from sources to buy one card or split across cards. The Imperium Row refills to five, so you may buy the replacement immediately if affordable. Acquired cards go face up into your discard pile.
answers.evidence: Acquiring Cards: Reveal purchases, pool/split, Row replacement, acquired card destination.

answers.answer: At an unoccupied Maker space, a spice is added to its bonus spot in Makers; when visiting, collect all bonus spice there, including when choosing worms. Deep Desert costs 3 water and offers 4 base spice or, with Hooks, two worms; Hagga Basin costs 1 water and offers 2 base spice or, with Hooks, one worm. Hooks are required only when the summoning effect specifies them and are not spent. The Shield Wall bars worms at Arrakeen, Spice Refinery, and Imperial Basin while present. Worms go directly into the Conflict and never into a garrison.
answers.evidence: Makers; Board Space Guide; Sandworms: Hooks and Shield Wall; bonus spice.

answers.answer: Endgame is triggered at Recall, at the end of a round, if any player has 10+ VP or the Conflict Deck is empty. Players first may play and resolve Endgame Intrigues, then most VP wins. Tiebreakers in order are spice, Solari, water, and garrisoned troops.
answers.evidence: Phase 5: Recall triggers Endgame; Scoring: Endgame Intrigue then VP and tiebreakers.

answers.answer: Standard CHOAM setup shuffles the 20 standard contracts and exposes 2 face up, leaving 18 face down in the bank. Add 4 Imperium and 4 Intrigue cards. Shaddam is optional. The 10 contrasting-back contracts are only for Rise of Ix compatibility and are not part of this standard setup. If Shaddam is chosen, the two Sardaukar contracts are set aside first; then 2 offers and 16 bank contracts are made from the remaining 18, with those two reserved separately.
answers.evidence: CHOAM Setup changes; Components: 10 contrasting-back contracts are Rise of Ix only.

answers.answer: With CHOAM and available contracts, the icon takes one face-up contract into your supply and replaces it from the bank. Without CHOAM, or when all contracts have been taken, it gives 2 Solari. Harvest completes by visiting a Maker space and gaining the contract’s stated total spice that turn, including other sources; Immediate completes on taking it; Acquire The Spice Must Flow completes when you next acquire that card.
answers.evidence: Taking contracts; Completing contracts; Board guide shared contract-icon rule.

answers.answer: No. You must hold a board-space contract when you send the Agent, so one taken after visiting waits until a future turn. On completion, announce it, gain its listed rewards, then flip it face down and leave it in your supply.
answers.evidence: Completing contracts: must have held contract when sending Agent; completion procedure.

answers.answer: Use one shared scoring Rival. The Rival gets the Ornithopter Objective; the humans randomly receive the other two eligible Objectives. First Player goes to the human whose Objective shows the marker. Turn order is First Player → Rival → other human; the Rival never Reveals.
answers.evidence: Required Rival Rules—Setup and Agent turns.

answers.answer: If the indicated board space is occupied, the Rival ignores it and reveals another Hagal card. A Place Spy card does not place an Agent: try an empty post of its specified type, ignore if none exists, then immediately reveal another card either way. Normal space costs and effects are ignored; apply only Hagal effects. If House Hagal empties or Reshuffle appears, reshuffle immediately and continue.
answers.evidence: Required Rival Rules—Agent turns and Place Spy cards.

answers.answer: Omit Objectives whose player-count marking does not match, shuffle eligible cards, and deal one face up to each player; the Objective’s First Player marker determines the first player. Shaddam may be chosen only when playing with CHOAM.
answers.evidence: Setup steps 3 and 5; Shaddam only with CHOAM.

answers.answer: Solari, spice, water and sandworms are not limited; make a convenient substitution if the bank runs out. Troops are different: if a player has no troops in supply, they cannot recruit more until troops return there. Resource payments return to the bank.
answers.evidence: Setup bank rules; Recruiting & Deploying Units.

answers.answer: The phases are Round Start, Player Turns, Combat, Makers, Recall. At Round Start reveal a Conflict, resolve any eligible defensive troop, then each player draws five cards. At Recall, if Endgame is not triggered, humans return Agents to Leaders; with 3–4 humans pass First Player clockwise, while in two-player play return Rival Agents to supply and pass First Player to the other human.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: phases 1–5 and Recall.

answers.answer: Yes, board-space effects, Agent-box effects, and the Faction Influence advance may be carried out in any order. But costs and requirements must be satisfied before placement; Influence gained from that visit cannot meet its own entry requirement.
answers.evidence: Agent Turn: pay costs and meet requirements before effects; effects may be in any order.

answers.answer: An optional arrow cost may be paid only once per turn; you cannot repeat it, except a sandworm may double a Conflict-card reward. Most card and space effects are mandatory. Exceptions include “may,” optional arrow costs, and the optional black-X trash icon; direct trash instructions are mandatory. Intrigue costs and conditions must be met to play it.
answers.evidence: Arrows / paying costs; FAQ—Mandatory effects and costs.

answers.answer: Place a Spy from supply on an unoccupied observation post. If you have none in supply, you may first recall one of your Spies for no effect. If the placement effect specifies an Agent-icon type, the post must connect to a space with that type; otherwise placement is not allowed.
answers.evidence: Spies & observation posts.

answers.answer: No: Infiltrate bypasses another player’s Agent, not your own. Recalling a Spy does not remove the need to play a card for the Agent turn. Two different connected Spies may pay for Infiltrate and Gather Intelligence together, but the same Spy cannot pay twice, and you cannot recall two Spies to Gather Intelligence on the same placement.
answers.evidence: Spies & observation posts; FAQ—Spies.

answers.answer: The controller gains the location’s bonus whenever any player, including the controller, visits: 1 Solari at Arrakeen or Spice Refinery, 1 spice at Imperial Basin. Winning the corresponding Conflict places your Control marker there and replaces the prior marker. The defensive troop comes from the controller’s supply and is deployed directly to the Conflict when that Conflict is revealed.
answers.evidence: Critical Locations & Control.

answers.answer: In a three-player tie for second, each tied player gets the third reward; the Conflict winner keeps first reward and the card, with no further rewards. Tied third-place players get nothing. If three players tie for first, each gets second reward and nobody takes the Conflict card; there are no other rewards, including in a four-player game.
answers.evidence: Combat ties and three-tied-first clarification.

answers.answer: With three different positive strengths in a three-player Conflict, first and second receive their printed rewards and third receives nothing. The third reward is used only for a tie for second in games with three or fewer players. A Rival counts as the third competitor in two-player play, so the same reward rule applies.
answers.evidence: Resolve Combat: player-count reward ranks; ordinary third receives nothing with 2–3 players.

answers.answer: Plot Intrigues may be played on your own Agent or Reveal turns; Combat Intrigues during Combat only if you have a unit in the Conflict; Endgame Intrigues at game end. Keep unplayed Intrigues face down, separate from your deck; after resolving a played Intrigue, put it face up in a discard pile by the Intrigue Deck. If the deck runs out, shuffle its discard to make a new deck.
answers.evidence: Intrigue cards; FAQ—Draw timing.

answers.answer: An ordinary discard instruction discards a card of your choice from your hand, and it cannot be an Intrigue unless specified. Secrets steals one Intrigue at random from each opponent who has four or more Intrigues.
answers.evidence: Discarding; Secrets board space; Steal Intrigue icon.

answers.answer: Trash effects may remove cards from hand, discard pile, or in play. Ordinary trashed cards return to the box; Reserve cards return to their Reserve stack. Trashing is optional unless it pays a cost or the card instructs you to trash itself. The Spice Must Flow’s acquire VP remains even if the card is later trashed.
answers.evidence: Trashing; FAQ—Victory.

answers.answer: Resolve an acquire-box effect once, at the moment the card is acquired. If unable to draw because your deck is empty, reshuffle your discard pile into a new deck and continue. Unused Persuasion cannot be saved and is lost after your Reveal turn.
answers.evidence: Acquire box; Acquiring Cards.

answers.answer: Cards played on Agent turns and revealed on Reveal turns remain face up and in play until Clean Up at the end of Reveal, unless trashed first. Fremen Bond works if you have one or more other Fremen cards in play; two Bond cards can activate each other regardless of play order.
answers.evidence: In play / Fremen Bond.

answers.answer: Recall Agent returns one of your other Agents on the board, not the Agent just sent; the recalled Agent may be used on another Agent turn in the same round. Retreat moves a troop from Conflict to garrison, and “retreat any number” includes zero.
answers.evidence: Recall Agent icon; Retreat; FAQ—Combat and troops.

answers.answer: A free-choice effect granting two Influence requires choosing one Faction for both; it cannot be split. An Alliance icon requires holding that Faction’s Alliance token. A minimum-Influence effect requires reaching its stated threshold.
answers.evidence: Influence: free-choice two gains; Alliance and minimum requirements.

answers.answer: If the Alliance holder loses Influence after being tied, the formerly tied opponent takes the token; if multiple opponents were tied, the former holder chooses its recipient. If the holder falls to 3 or lower and nobody has 4+, return the token to the board; the former holder loses the token’s VP.
answers.evidence: Faction Influence; FAQ—Alliance loss.

answers.answer: A card drawn during Reveal is immediately revealed and used this turn. A card drawn after Reveal stays for next round, when you draw five additional cards. A Plot Intrigue with a later Reveal effect remains face up until then, is used, then discarded.
answers.evidence: FAQ—Draw timing.

answers.answer: No. A “when you win” Intrigue cannot be played after tying for first. If you receive one as a reward for an outright win, you may play it immediately.
answers.evidence: FAQ—Combat and troops.

answers.answer: If VP and all four resource tiebreakers remain tied, the player who most recently took a Reveal turn wins. Scores may exceed 12.
answers.evidence: FAQ—Victory.

answers.answer: No. Fulfill all contracts you hold for the same space with one Agent placement; you must have held them when sending the Agent. Contract completion is another effect of that Agent turn and may resolve in any order with space and Agent-box effects.
answers.evidence: FAQ—Contract completion is mandatory.

answers.answer: Shaddam does not begin with the reserved Sardaukar contracts. Only Shaddam may acquire them, choosing one instead of a generally available contract when acquiring. His Signet Ring deployment restriction takes effect immediately when playing Signet Ring to send an Agent and lasts for that turn, not the round.
answers.evidence: CHOAM—Reserved Sardaukar contracts; Shaddam’s Signet benefits; FAQ—Shaddam.

answers.answer: Feyd’s token starts on the leftmost space of his Training track and stays on the rightmost space once it reaches it. Lady Jessica side begins face up. Reverend Mother Jessica may use her ability on the turn she flips.
answers.evidence: Leader clarifications; FAQ—Reverend Mother Jessica.

answers.answer: Moving from 1 to 3 counts as reaching 2; after dropping below 2, moving back up through 2 can count again. Moving down through 2 does not count. Clean Up moving Spacing Guild’s Favor from play to discard does not trigger its discard ability; only discarding it from hand does.
answers.evidence: Leader clarifications: Margot/Irulan and Spacing Guild’s Favor.

answers.answer: Accept Contract uses Spice Trade, has no cost, is not a Combat space, and always draws one card; its contract icon gives 2 Solari without CHOAM or when contracts are exhausted, otherwise takes a contract. It gives no automatic Faction Influence. Dutiful Service uses Emperor, has no cost, is not a Combat space, gives one Emperor Influence total, plus the same contract-icon effect.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide: contract-space faction status, shared icon rule, table.

answers.answer: Arrakeen: City icon, no cost, Combat yes; visitor recruits one troop and draws one card, while controller gets 1 Solari. Fremkit: Fremen icon, no cost, Combat yes; gain 1 Fremen Influence and draw a card. Research Station: City icon, costs 2 water, Combat yes; recruit two troops and draw two cards.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide table: Arrakeen, Fremkit, Research Station.

answers.answer: Deep Desert costs 3 water and offers 4 base spice or, with Maker Hooks, two sandworms. Hagga Basin costs 1 water and offers 2 base spice or, with Hooks, one sandworm. At either space you still gain all accumulated bonus spice when choosing worms. Hooks are retained, not spent.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide: Deep Desert and Hagga Basin; Sandworms.

answers.answer: Both options require City access and 2+ Fremen Influence, with no resource entry cost; the space permits Combat deployment. First option: take Maker Hooks if lacking them, recruit one troop, and gain 1 water. Second: gain 1 water and optionally remove the Shield Wall. The second option grants no troop.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide: Sietch Tabr.

answers.answer: High Council uses Landsraad, is not a Combat space, and costs 5 Solari each visit. First visit places your Councilor on an unoccupied seat and grants 2 Persuasion on every Reveal turn for the rest of the game. Later visits give 2 spice, draw an Intrigue, and recruit three troops.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide: High Council.

answers.answer: Swordmaster costs 8 Solari before anyone gains one, then 6 Solari once anyone has one; this changes if a Rival gains it too. Each player may take it only once per game. The third Agent becomes available this round and for the rest of the game.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide: Swordmaster.

answers.answer: Imperial Privilege uses Landsraad, requires 2+ Emperor Influence, costs 3 Solari, and is not a Combat space. Its effects allow discarding an Intrigue to draw an Intrigue, and recalling one of your other Agents to draw a card. It does not automatically grant Emperor Influence.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide: Imperial Privilege.

answers.answer: Shipping uses Spice Trade, requires 2+ Guild Influence, costs 3 spice, and is not a Combat space. It grants 5 Solari and 1 Influence with any one Faction; that Influence need not be Guild.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide: Shipping.

answers.answer: Gather Support is Landsraad, not Combat: choose to pay 0 or 2 Solari, recruit two troops either way, and gain 1 water if you paid 2. Spice Refinery is City, Combat yes: choose to pay 0 or 1 spice and gain 2 or 4 Solari respectively; its controller also gains 1 Solari.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide: Gather Support and Spice Refinery.

answers.answer: Heighliner: 5 spice, Spacing Guild, +1 Guild Influence and recruit five troops; Combat yes. Desert Tactics: 1 water, Fremen, +1 Fremen Influence, recruit one troop, optionally trash a card; Combat yes. Sardaukar: 4 spice, Emperor, +1 Emperor Influence, draw an Intrigue and recruit four troops; Combat no.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide table: Heighliner, Desert Tactics, Sardaukar.

answers.answer: Assembly Hall: Landsraad, no cost, not Combat; draw an Intrigue and gain 1 Persuasion during Reveal if your Agent is there. Espionage: Bene Gesserit, costs 1 spice, not Combat; gain 1 Bene Gesserit Influence, draw a card, place a Spy. Deliver Supplies: Spacing Guild, no cost, not Combat; gain 1 Guild Influence and 1 water.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide table: Assembly Hall, Espionage, Deliver Supplies.

answers.answer: False Orders makes affected opponents move their Spy to an empty post not connected to your Agent’s destination that turn; it may be played even if no enemy Spy is connected there. Litany Against Fear’s red box is ignored during Reveal, or when its gained Agent icon lets it be played as an Agent card.
answers.evidence: FAQ: False Orders; Litany Against Fear.

answers.answer: With Manipulate, opponents cannot acquire the removed card. You may acquire it by other means, but without the 1-Persuasion discount. If still unacquired by the end of your next Reveal, remove it from the game.
answers.evidence: FAQ—Manipulate.

answers.answer: The Rival starts with four Influence cubes at track bottoms, three troops in its garrison and remaining troops in supply, two Agents and three Spies in supply, and 1 water; its score and Combat marker are 0, and Swordmaster is beside the board. Shuffle House Hagal and put it near the Rival, retaining the 2P Reshuffle card. The Rival can trigger Endgame at 10+ VP and can win.
answers.evidence: Required Rival Rules—Setup; components and scoring rule.

answers.answer: Count Solari, spice, Intrigue cards and water together, each unit as one. As soon as the total reaches its printed Swordmaster threshold, spend that amount; spend Solari first, then spice, Intrigue cards, then water, keeping leftovers. The third Agent is usable in the current round.
answers.evidence: Required Rival Rules—Resources and Swordmaster.

answers.answer: After Swordmaster, the Rival spends each exact set of 7 Solari, 7 spice, 3 Intrigue cards, or 3 water for 1 VP. It cannot use a mixed total of seven different resources for a VP.
answers.evidence: Required Rival Rules—Resources and Swordmaster.

answers.answer: The Rival chooses the Faction with least Influence and breaks ties by its leftmost priority icon. It gains VP at 2 Influence and gains Alliance VP like a human, but does not receive the resource bonus for reaching 4. A numbered Hagal Influence icon refers to that position on its priority list.
answers.evidence: Required Rival Rules—Resources and Swordmaster; Influence selection.

answers.answer: For two-destination cards, the conditions select only one destination: Guild Influence for Accept Contract/Shipping, or Conflict tier for Deliver Supplies/Heighliner. If the selected destination is occupied, reveal another card; do not use the other destination.
answers.evidence: Required Rival Rules—Agent turns.

answers.answer: At a Combat space the Rival deploys up to two available garrison troops even when the card recruited none. Troops recruited at a noncombat space go to its garrison. An unmet conditional 2+ Influence bonus does not prevent placing the Agent.
answers.evidence: Required Rival Rules—Agent turns: troop icons and conditional bonuses.

answers.answer: Unless a post type is specified, the Rival places a Spy at the first available Faction post in priority order; if all four are occupied, it ignores placement. Placing its third and final supply Spy recalls the other two and triggers its Scheme. Rivals never recall Spies for Infiltrate or Gather Intelligence.
answers.evidence: Required Rival Rules—Spies and Schemes.

answers.answer: If its Scheme recruits troops before Agent placement and the Rival then visits a Combat space that turn, those troops deploy too. If a Place Spy card has no legal empty post, ignore placement and immediately reveal another Hagal card because no Agent was sent.
answers.evidence: Required Rival Rules—Spies and Schemes; Place Spy cards.

answers.answer: At either Maker space the Rival collects all bonus spice. With Hooks and a Conflict that permits worms, it summons one worm at Hagga Basin or two at Deep Desert instead of taking base spice. Without Hooks, or when the Conflict is protected, it takes base spice instead: 2 at Hagga, 4 at Deep Desert. Hooks are retained.
answers.evidence: Required Rival Rules—Maker spaces; Hooks and Wall icons.

answers.answer: At Combat start, if the Rival has at least one deployed unit, reveal a Hagal card and add its bottom swords to strength; on Reshuffle, reshuffle and reveal again. Humans then have their normal Combat Intrigue window. A unit-free Rival gets no bonus.
answers.evidence: Required Rival Rules—Combat.

answers.answer: The Rival can gain control, defensive troops, battle-icon VP, and doubled Conflict rewards with worms. Always take an optional Conflict VP if it can pay or recall the required Spies. It never takes contracts; a contract reward gives 2 Solari even with CHOAM.
answers.evidence: Required Rival Rules—Combat.

answers.answer: During Reveal, total and announce strength and set the marker at any point while resolving; update it as needed, including when a Combat Intrigue changes strength during its resolution. Combat uses the adjusted strength on the track. Above 20, flip the marker to its +20 side and start again from the beginning.
answers.evidence: Reveal Turn; Combat; Strength.

answers.answer: A Leader’s Signet Ring ability activates when you play Signet Ring on one of your Agent turns, not when you merely reveal it. Cards of any type can override the usual rules of the game.
answers.evidence: Setup, step 3: Leader Signet Ring; Overview: cards can override rules.

answers.answer: A Recall Spy icon returns one of your Spies from a post to your supply, generally as a cost for an effect. It is not automatically Infiltrate or Gather Intelligence; those are separate choices when sending an Agent.
answers.evidence: Spies & observation posts.

answers.answer: The separate trash-an-Intrigue icon trashes one Intrigue of your choice from your hand. An ordinary discard instruction discards a card from hand but cannot discard an Intrigue unless it specifies one.
answers.evidence: Trashing; Discarding.

answers.answer: A sandworm-doubled reward granting one Influence of your choice can yield two Influence, with the same Faction or two different Factions. This differs from a single effect granting two free-choice Influence, which must place both on one Faction.
answers.evidence: Sandworm Reward Doubling; Influence.

answers.answer: Resolve the Rival card’s printed Signet Ring ability. Do not substitute its Scheme. It requires neither a human Signet Ring card nor a Reveal turn.
answers.evidence: Required Rival Rules—Rival Signet Ring and Scheme.

answers.answer: A Maker Hooks icon gives the Rival one token if it lacks Hooks and does nothing if it already has one. A Shield Wall removal effect removes the Wall only if the Rival has Hooks and the Wall remains; without Hooks it is ignored, and if the Wall is already gone there is no further effect.
answers.evidence: Required Rival Rules—Rival Hooks and Wall icons.

answers.answer: Secrets uses Bene Gesserit, has no cost, and is not a Combat space. It gives 1 Bene Gesserit Influence and draws an Intrigue from the deck; each opponent holding 4+ Intrigues gives one selected at random.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide: Secrets; Steal Intrigue icon.

answers.answer: Imperial Basin uses Spice Trade, has no cost, and is a Combat space. Visitor gets 1 base spice plus all bonus spice; its controller gets 1 spice. If the visitor also controls it, it gets both the visitor’s spice and the controller’s 1 spice.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide: Imperial Basin; controlled-location visit rule.

answers.answer: At Round Start, reveal the new Conflict and place it face up next to the deck, on top of any unclaimed Conflict cards from earlier rounds. Then each player draws five cards.
answers.evidence: Phase 1: Round Start.

answers.answer: Place each human’s four Influence cubes on the bottom spaces of the four Faction tracks. Alliance tokens begin on the marked areas of those tracks; no player begins holding one. The Shield Wall token begins on the board below Spice Refinery.
answers.evidence: Setup steps 1 and 6; Maker Hooks bank setup.

answers.answer: The First Player starts; play proceeds clockwise one turn at a time. A player who Reveals is skipped thereafter, and in normal 3–4-player play Player Turns ends once all players have Revealed. Combat Intrigue priority starts with First Player and proceeds clockwise; an eligible player with a unit may play any number or pass, and the window closes after all involved players pass consecutively.
answers.evidence: Phase 2: Player Turns; Phase 3: Combat Intrigue.

answers.answer: The steps are Reveal Cards (reveal all cards remaining in hand), Resolve Reveal Effects (resolve those cards’ Reveal boxes), and Clean Up (move all cards in front of you to discard). Reveal effects may be resolved in any order.
answers.evidence: Reveal Turn: three steps.

answers.answer: Shuffle each human’s 10-card starter deck and place it face down in their supply left of Leader. Without CHOAM, omit CHOAM cards; shuffle the Intrigue and Imperium decks separately face down and deal five Imperium cards face up for the Row; place Prepare the Way and The Spice Must Flow in separate Reserve stacks. Human Combat marker starts at 0; three Spies, Councilor and Control markers remain in supply.
answers.evidence: Setup steps 4 and 6; Initial card states.

answers.answer: During Reveal, Persuasion may buy any of five Imperium Row cards or either Reserve card, Prepare the Way or The Spice Must Flow. The cost is at the card’s top right. Ordinary Persuasion purchases are made during your Reveal turn.
answers.evidence: Acquiring Cards.

answers.answer: Ordinary Spy placement and Recall Spy icons are optional even if a legal placement or recall exists. The Shield Wall detonation icon may remove the Wall; removal is permanent and it cannot return in a later round.
answers.evidence: Spies & observation posts; Shield Wall.

answers.answer: Normally the played card must have an Agent icon matching the destination. A connected Spy alone does not let a City-only card access Shipping. If the card has the Spy Agent icon and your Spy is at a connected post, it can access the connected destination without recalling the Spy.
answers.evidence: Agent Turn; Spies & observation posts.

answers.answer: Yes. On an Agent turn you may first play a legal Plot Intrigue; resources it grants before placement can pay the entry cost. Resources from the card played to send the Agent, or from the destination, are gained only after placement and cannot pay that same entry cost.
answers.evidence: Player Turns: Plot Intrigue and entry-cost timing; Agent Turn.

answers.answer: No. After both humans Reveal, continue the Rival’s Agent turns while it still has Agents in supply; Player Turns ends only after both humans Revealed and the Rival used all its Agents. The Rival never takes a Reveal turn.
answers.evidence: Phase 2: two-player Player Turns.

answers.answer:

| Accept Contract | Spice Trade | No |
| Arrakeen | City | Yes |
| Assembly Hall | Landsraad | No |
| Deep Desert | Spice Trade | Yes |
| Deliver Supplies | Spacing Guild | No |
| Desert Tactics | Fremen | Yes |
| Dutiful Service | Emperor | No |

answers.answer: When the Conflict is revealed, a player already controlling that location may deploy one troop from supply directly to the Conflict; it is optional and requires no Agent visit. After rewards, Combat markers reset to 0 before the next phase.
answers.evidence: Phase 1: defensive troop bonus; Phase 3: Combat cleanup.

answers.answer: Play one card from your hand face up in front of you and send one Agent from your Leader to an unoccupied matching space; resolve its Agent box, not Reveal box. You cannot reuse a card already in play or discard, or move an Agent already on the board as the sent Agent.
answers.evidence: Agent Turn.

answers.answer: The restriction applies immediately when Shaddam plays Signet Ring to send the Agent; he cannot order board effects first to deploy units before it starts.
answers.evidence: Leader clarifications—Shaddam; CHOAM Shaddam Signet benefits.

answers.answer: With four different positive strengths, first, second, and third place receive the corresponding printed rewards; fourth receives none. The highest-strength player wins and takes the Conflict card face up, then checks it for a battle-icon match.
answers.evidence: Resolve Combat: four-player ranks; winner card procedure.

answers.answer: Players may choose a Leader or select one at random.
answers.evidence: Setup, step 3.

answers.answer: An ordinary draw-a-card effect draws from your own deck. You may not choose a card directly from your discard pile; if your deck is empty, shuffle discard into a new deck and draw.
answers.evidence: Drawing cards.

answers.answer: Shuffle House Hagal and place the deck near the shared Rival, retaining the 2P Reshuffle card.
answers.evidence: Required Rival Rules—Setup.

answers.answer: All four Maker Hooks tokens begin in the common bank; normal setup assigns none to a human. When a player later takes one, it moves from the bank onto that player’s garrison.
answers.evidence: Setup step 7.

answers.answer: When the Combat Intrigue resolves and changes deployed units or strength, adjust that participant’s Combat marker during the Combat Intrigue window. Combat rewards use the adjusted strength shown on the track, not a fixed Reveal value.
answers.evidence: Phase 3: Combat Intrigue.

answers.answer: Gain Solari, spice or water from the bank, not another player’s supply.
answers.evidence: Setup step 7.

answers.answer: Shuffle all 20 standard contract tokens face down, then flip two face up for the offers and keep the rest face down in the bank. Players do not choose the offers or preset the bank order.
answers.evidence: CHOAM Setup changes: shuffle contracts, flip two face up, rest face down.

answers.answer: Set aside both Sardaukar contracts before shuffling. Only Shaddam may acquire them, and setting them aside does not give him possession. Shuffle the other 18, expose two as public offers, and put the remaining 16 face down in the bank, with the two reserved contracts separate.
answers.evidence: CHOAM Setup changes; Reserved Sardaukar contracts.
